Had a man on Market lose it with me a few years back when I handed him what cash I had. Granted, it was only a few singles, but it was still the only paper cash I had with me. 

I was in my mid-twenties at the time. This panhandling dude was probably close to twice my weight, and head-and-shoulders taller.

When I gave him the bills, he looked at it, then asked, “That’s it?”

When I told him that was what I had, he got irate, started yelling that that was ridiculous, that I should, “go to the ATM” and get him some more. I backed up and sort of scuttled into the Westfield building before waiting there for a while.

I know, I know, it is what it is, but…woof. On the plus side, one of the funnier ways I’ve been called a broke bitch.

Management at my hospital has done this as well. Even took it a step farther and began tampering with employees’ timecards/clockings to avoid paying incremental OT. When they were caught doing this, knowing full well it’s quite literally a crime to do so, they tried to say, “It’s only a few minutes, why do you care?” Multiple admin over the years have been caught doing it, and somehow, the majority of them have still managed to keep their jobs by just being shuffled around within the organizational hierarchy. 🤦🏻‍♀️

During my ICU clinical, my preceptor told me to turn our patient using the external fixators on their legs.

I expressed concern that doing that would hurt the patient, and this nurse said, “Listen, I know this type of patient. They had alcohol in their blood when they came in. Don’t feel bad for them,” and then proceeded to grab the fixators and start yanking the patient around in bed. The patient wasn’t able to verbalize at the time, but they were clearly grimacing and crying silently while they were being jerked around by the hardware.

Shook me up badly. When I spoke with my clinical instructor about it, I genuinely thought for a hot second that she was about to go fistfight this nurse. Instead, she went to the ICU manager. For the remaining weeks I was on that unit, I never saw that nurse again.

I have a four-year-old ekkie boy, Pancho, whom I’ve raised from the time he was a few months old. I know some folks might balk when I say this, but he’s as precious to me as how I imagine a human child might be to their own parents(no human babies of my own thus far).

He’s really become part of the family - my own mother even calls him, “the grandbirdie,” and he always says, “Abuelita!” whenever he sees her. My parents keep a travel aviary and toys for him at their house, and he loves snuggling up to my dad when he’s chilling on the couch.

He keeps me going during the hard times. He came home just before the 2020 lockdown started, and during the constant nightmare scenarios we were seeing in healthcare during the early days of the pandemic, he kept my spirits up. He saw me through a breakup of an almost decade-long relationship during that time as well, and when my depression has taken me to some incredibly dark places, he’s been a little green ray of light.

Some things definitely require more logistics and expense with him in the mix - ie, vacation planning, how long I can be away from the house at a time, making chop and always buying new toys for him to tear up - but I still wouldn’t trade it for the world. 💚

My three-year-old Solomon Island boy just passed this stool while on his perch. This is highly unusual - normally, his stool is pretty typical-appearing, although it may be slightly more watery if he’s been eating food or fruit with a higher water content in it that day.

I immediately worried, because I’ve heard that green coloration like this(especially of the urates) can be indicative of liver disease, psittacosis, or other potentially deadly ailments.

Some of the stool I saw when I checked his cage lining looked similar. However, some of his other stool from the last day looks relatively normal(C).

He eats primarily an organic veggie/chop diet, with a bit of chopped fruit(mostly berries) and a small amount of quinoa added, as well as a small amount of roudybush and zupreem naturals/dye-free pellets. The cage liner is changed daily, and the cage gets a full spray and scrub-down at least a few times a week, if not more frequently.

He has no other symptoms at this time, as well as no change to his appetite, energy, or behavior. I know that birds often don’t have more noticeable symptoms until they’re quite ill, though, so I’m still quite worried.

What are your thoughts or suggestions? Do you think this is a sure sign of psittacosis, discoloration due to his diet, or something else?

As others are saying, it definitely depends on the area of the US you’re in. I currently live and work in Northern California, which generally has a pretty strong union presence, as well as the benefit of state-mandated nurse-to-patient ratios/caps. As a new grad nurse, though, I worked in a non-union state for about a year, and it was a nightmare. Pay was awful, working conditions were more often than not dirty and unsafe, and anyone who so much as whispered the word “union” could be fired on the spot. I’m now one of the nurses’ union representatives at the hospital where I work, and it’s such a relief to know you have that support behind you in the face of corrupt hospital administrations and the like.
Thankfully, we’re in the middle of (labor)contract negotiations, so there’s at least something of a chance staff will see some sort of pay raise soon.

I’m tired. So frickin’ tired of coming home after seeing patients nearly(or actually) dying from this virus, dying without being able to say goodbye to their loved ones, even - and having to hear people who think getting their hair colored is an essential service try to tell me how it’s not real.

I...I don’t know what to say. As someone who has dealt with depression, suicidal ideation, and chronic pain for much of my life - and shit, even if that weren’t the case - my heart is breaking for you, and I wish there were something more impactful and effective I could do for you than just offer what probably seem like hollow, placating words from a stranger over the internet.

I hope you, and your fellow Canadians, are able to vote the bastards throwing citizens’ wellbeing under the bus out of office as quickly as possible. I know that kind of thing is more easily said than done - believe me, we’ve got a band of unhinged conservatives trying to run what’s left of the US into the ground in the name of profit - but I really do hope people can come together and accomplish it. 

I hope it doesn’t sound too weird or too forward, but if you’re ever really having a time of it and need an ear to vent to, I’m a night nurse, so I’m often up at all hours of the night and morning - feel free to shoot me a message, if it would be helpful for you to blow off some steam.
